---
title: "Stack an auditory-language hierarchy"
subtitle: "One speech wav becomes acoustics, prosody, phonology, and semantics on a single shared grid."
sidebar: cookbook
---

## Use when

You want every level of a hierarchical auditory-language analysis rendered onto
one time grid, so the levels stack into a single design matrix with per-level
column blocks. That layout is what banded ridge regression, hierarchical
regression, and variance partitioning across the speech hierarchy need.

| Level | Block | What it captures | Extractors |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `acoustic.*` | Envelope, spectrum, cepstrum | `rms`, `mel`, `mfcc`, `spectral_stats`, `gammatone` |
| 2 | `prosody.*` | F0, voicing, energy dynamics | `audio_pitch`, `prosody_features` |
| 3 | `phonology.*` | Phone-class posteriors, articulatory features | `extract_acoustic_phonetics` |
| 4 | `semantic.*` | Sentence/paragraph embeddings, lexical controls | `extract_multiscale_language` |

The executed cells use a short synthetic waveform and an inline transcript so
this page renders with no model downloads. Every extractor shown here is the
same one you would call on a real recording.

## One canonical grid

Each level produces `FeatureSeries` on its own native grid. Rendering all of
them through a single `build_tr_grid` grid is what makes them stackable.

```{python}
import tempfile
import wave
from pathlib import Path

import numpy as np

from natural_features.core.feature_types import FeatureSeries
from natural_features.core.stimulus import AudioStimulus
from natural_features.fmri.resample import build_tr_grid, resample_feature_series

sr_hz = 16000
duration_s = 16.0
tr_s = 1.0  # analysis resolution; use your scan TR for fMRI

# A speech-like carrier: a syllable-rate amplitude envelope on a voiced buzz.
t = np.arange(int(duration_s * sr_hz), dtype=np.float32) / sr_hz
envelope = 0.2 + 0.18 * np.sin(2.0 * np.pi * 4.0 * t)
carrier = np.sin(2.0 * np.pi * 130.0 * t) + 0.5 * np.sin(2.0 * np.pi * 260.0 * t)
samples = (envelope * carrier).astype(np.float32)

tmpdir = tempfile.TemporaryDirectory()
wav_path = Path(tmpdir.name) / "speech_like.wav"
pcm = np.asarray(np.clip(samples, -1.0, 1.0) * 32767.0, dtype="<i2")
with wave.open(str(wav_path), "wb") as wav:
    wav.setnchannels(1)
    wav.setsampwidth(2)
    wav.setframerate(sr_hz)
    wav.writeframes(pcm.tobytes())

audio = AudioStimulus.from_wav(wav_path)
total_s = audio.start_offset_s + audio.samples.shape[0] / audio.sr_hz
grid = build_tr_grid(duration_s=total_s, tr_s=tr_s, start_s=audio.start_offset_s)


def on_grid(fs, method="mean"):
    return resample_feature_series(fs, tr_s=tr_s, method=method, time_grid_s=grid)


def prefixed(fs, prefix):
    names = [str(n) for n in fs.coords.get("feature", [])]
    return FeatureSeries(
        values=fs.values,
        times_s=fs.times_s,
        dims=fs.dims,
        coords={"feature": [f"{prefix}{n}" for n in names]},
        metadata=fs.metadata,
        timebase=fs.timebase,
        time_bounds_s=fs.time_bounds_s,
        temporal_context=fs.temporal_context,
    )


grid
```

## Level 1: low-level acoustics

```{python}
from natural_features.features.audio.lowlevel import mfcc, rms, spectral_stats

acoustic = [
    prefixed(on_grid(rms(audio)), "acoustic.rms."),
    prefixed(
        on_grid(mfcc(audio, n_mfcc=13, n_mels=40, include_deltas=True)),
        "acoustic.mfcc.",
    ),
    prefixed(on_grid(spectral_stats(audio)), "acoustic.spectral."),
]
[fs.values.shape for fs in acoustic]
```

For batches of clips, `extract_audio_files` wraps the same extractors plus
`mel`, `pitch`, `prosody`, `vad`, and openSMILE eGeMAPS; see
[Extract audio features from WAV files](audio-batch-from-wav.qmd).

## Level 2: prosody

```{python}
from natural_features.features.audio.prosody import prosody_features

prosody = [prefixed(on_grid(prosody_features(audio)), "prosody.")]
list(prosody[0].coords["feature"])
```

`audio_pitch` is available separately when only F0 and voicing are needed.

## Level 3: phonetics and phonology

`posterior_backend="acoustic"` is a deterministic coarse-class mapping that
needs no model weights, which is what keeps this page renderable.

```{python}
from natural_features.workflows import extract_acoustic_phonetics

phon = extract_acoustic_phonetics(audio, posterior_backend="acoustic")
phonology = [
    prefixed(on_grid(phon.posteriorgrams), "phonology.post."),
    prefixed(on_grid(phon.articulatory), "phonology.artic."),
]
[fs.values.shape for fs in phonology]
```

On real speech you would usually want the strict neural backend instead. The
CTC model loads once per process and is reused across files, and audio longer
than `chunk_window_s` is chunked with overlap automatically:

```python
phon = extract_acoustic_phonetics(
    audio,
    posterior_backend="ctc",      # strict wav2vec2 phoneme-CTC model
    ctc_device="auto",            # CUDA, then MPS, then CPU
    ctc_local_files_only=True,    # reproducible/offline
)
```

`posterior_backend="ppgs"` wraps phonetic posteriorgrams as a third option.
Details for all three live in the
[acoustic phonetics quickstart](../acoustic_phonetics_quickstart.md).

## Level 4: sentence- and paragraph-level semantics

Words come from your transcript with uniform timing, or from strict Whisper ASR
when you omit `transcript_text`. Sentence and paragraph events are segmented
from the word stream, embedded per unit, then rendered onto the same grid.

```{python}
from natural_features.workflows import extract_multiscale_language

transcript = (
    "The tide came in slowly that morning. Gulls argued over the wet stones. "
    "A fishing boat idled past the breakwater.\n\n"
    "By noon the wind had turned. Rain moved across the harbour in sheets. "
    "Nobody stayed to watch it arrive."
)

language = extract_multiscale_language(
    audio,
    transcript_text=transcript,
    scales_s=[tr_s],
    feature_families=[
        "sentence_embeddings",
        "paragraph_embeddings",
        "lexical_controls",
    ],
    provider_config={"provider": "local_bow", "dim": 64},
    standardize=False,
    add_intercept=False,
)

semantic_dm = language.by_scale[tr_s]
if len(semantic_dm.times_s) != len(grid) or not np.allclose(semantic_dm.times_s, grid):
    # ASR or transcript word onsets can start after t=0; re-render onto the grid.
    semantic_dm = on_grid(semantic_dm, method="nearest")
semantic = [prefixed(semantic_dm, "semantic.")]

language.qc
```

`provider="local_bow"` is the offline bag-of-words provider used here. On real
data you would swap in a contextual provider:

```python
provider_config={"provider": "openai", "model": "text-embedding-3-large"}
```

Adding `"surprisal"` to `feature_families` contributes word-level
predictability from a causal language model. Unlike the three families above it
is a strict neural backend: it needs `transformers`, `torch`, and local weights,
and raises rather than substituting a proxy.

`language.words`, `language.sentences`, and `language.paragraphs` expose the
underlying `EventSeries` if you want event-locked rather than gridded designs.

## Stack into one hierarchical design

```{python}
from natural_features.fmri.design import concat_feature_series

blocks = {
    "acoustic": acoustic,
    "prosody": prosody,
    "phonology": phonology,
    "semantic": semantic,
}
design = concat_feature_series(
    [fs for level in blocks.values() for fs in level],
    standardize=True,
    add_intercept=False,
)

block_slices = {}
cursor = 0
for level, feats in blocks.items():
    width = sum(fs.values.shape[1] for fs in feats)
    block_slices[level] = (cursor, cursor + width)
    cursor += width

{
    "rows": int(design.values.shape[0]),
    "columns": int(design.values.shape[1]),
    "block_slices": block_slices,
}
```

`concat_feature_series` refuses to stack blocks whose grids, clocks, or window
supports disagree, so a misaligned level fails loudly instead of silently
shifting time.

```{python}
#| echo: false
tmpdir.cleanup()
```

## Run it end to end

[`examples/auditory_language_hierarchy.py`](https://github.com/bbuchsbaum/natural-features/blob/main/examples/auditory_language_hierarchy.py)
is the scripted version of this page. It records `block_slices` in a JSON
sidecar so downstream banded models can address each level by name:

```bash
python examples/auditory_language_hierarchy.py \
    --audio-wav tests/stimuli/tier_a/audio_speechlike.wav \
    --transcript tests/stimuli/tier_a/transcript_reference.txt \
    --resolution-s 1.0 \
    --out-prefix hierarchy_demo
```

Neural backends are opt-in flags on the same script: `--posterior-backend ctc`
for phone posteriors and `--surprisal lm` for language-model predictability.

## Notes

- **Determinism.** A transcript plus `posterior_backend="acoustic"` plus
  `provider="local_bow"` runs with no model downloads, which is what the
  integration test exercises.
- **Strict by default.** Neural backends (CTC, PPGs, Whisper ASR, API embedding
  providers, language-model surprisal) fail loudly when unavailable rather than
  substituting a proxy. Substitutes are always an explicit choice.
- **fMRI.** Set `tr_s` to your scan TR and map stimulus time onto scan time with
  a `ClockMap`; see [Sample RMS energy onto a TR grid](rms-energy-to-tr-grid.qmd).
  HRF convolution and lagging belong in your modeling layer.
- **Finer phonetic timing.** For event-locked phoneme analyses, align words with
  `whisperx_align`, expand to phones with `phoneme_events_from_words`, and map to
  articulatory features with `articulatory_from_phoneme_events`.
